topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing for the cancer biology lecture series, outlining course objectives and learning outcomes.

topics.label: Biological foundations: Genetic changes, tissue architecture, and differentiation failure
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the fundamental concept of cancer as a failure of cellular differentiation and tissue architecture driven by accumulating genetic and epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Tumour invasion, metastasis, and benign versus malignant progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the clinical and histological distinctions between benign and malignant tumours, focusing on basement membrane invasion, metastatic dissemination, and stepwise progression pathways.

topics.label: Tumour nomenclature conventions and exceptions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic defines the standard naming rules and notable exceptions used to classify benign and malignant tumours based on their cellular lineage and tissue of origin.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer-related morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the physiological mechanisms, including mechanical obstruction, tissue destruction, and systemic metabolic effects, through which tumours cause clinical illness and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence patterns across human tissues and animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine epidemiological incidence and mortality rates across human organs and compare tumour prevalence across multicellular animal taxa.

topics.label: Cancer screening rationale, methods, and clinical applications
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the principles of early tumour detection and evaluate specific screening tools, histological criteria, and clinical trade-offs across different organ sites.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing for the session, concluding the lecture and setting expectations for practical classes.
